claims.text: The undoped multi-component molten alloy readily crystallizes upon cooling.
Adding a minor concentration of boron enhances the glass-forming ability of a multi-component alloy.
Boron addition impedes crystallization during rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching from the melt produces deep undercooling and can bypass crystallization.
Boron atoms induce local chemical short-range order in the alloy.
Boron creates significant atomic-size mismatch in the alloy.
Boron has a large atomic-size difference relative to the alloy's main constituents.
Boron has a strongly negative heat of mixing with the alloy's main constituents.
The size mismatch and negative heat of mixing caused by boron disrupt the nucleation kinetics of crystalline phases.
Disruption of crystalline-phase nucleation kinetics kinetically retards crystallization.
The boron-doped alloy will have a higher amorphous-phase fraction than the undoped alloy under identical quenching conditions.
A higher amorphous-phase fraction indicates enhanced glass-forming ability.
The undoped alloy has a higher tendency to crystallize than the boron-doped alloy under identical rapid-quenching conditions.
The beneficial effect of boron is limited to minor concentrations compatible with the alloy system.
Excessive or incompatible boron addition can trigger unwanted secondary phases.
Metalloid doping with boron is expected to enhance glass formation on the basis of atomic-size mismatch and mixing-enthalpy considerations.
